problem.headline: Production infra is painful. It doesn't have to be.
problem.subheadline: Every time you ship something new, you solve the same problems: SSL setup, reverse proxy config, container health checks, log aggregation, backup jobs. None of this is the actual product.

points.title: docker-compose is production-capable — but nobody ships a hardened setup
points.body: Most tutorials stop at 'it works locally'. Getting SSL, health checks, restart policies, and log rotation right takes days of trial and error on a live server.

points.title: Monitoring is an afterthought until the server goes down at 2am
points.body: Standing up Prometheus, connecting Grafana, writing alert rules, wiring Alertmanager to Telegram — it's 3–4 days of work that has nothing to do with your product.

points.title: Backups are always 'I'll do it later'
points.body: PostgreSQL dumps, volume snapshots, offsite storage, retention policies. Easy to skip, catastrophic to miss.

points.title: Small teams don't need Kubernetes — they need a production-ready VPS
points.body: K8s is overkill for a single-product startup. A well-structured docker-compose stack handles 99% of early production workloads with a fraction of the operational cost.

steps.title: Provision a VPS
steps.body: Any Ubuntu 22.04 VPS — DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Vultr. 2 vCPU / 4GB RAM minimum.

steps.title: Clone the repo
steps.body: git clone and copy .env.example. Fill in your domain, credentials, and notification tokens.

steps.title: Run install.sh
steps.body: Bootstrap script installs Docker, configures firewall rules, sets up systemd service, and pulls images.

steps.title: Production ready
steps.body: SSL is live, monitoring is collecting metrics, backups are scheduled, Telegram alerts are firing.

aboutPage.headline: I build infrastructure tooling, automation systems, and startup products.
paragraphs: I'm a technical founder focused on the infrastructure layer of software products — the pieces that make systems reliable, observable, and easy to operate.
Most of what I build starts as internal tooling for my own products. When something is genuinely useful and solves a problem I see other founders hitting repeatedly, I productize it.
The goal is to give small teams production-grade infrastructure without the overhead of a dedicated DevOps function.
